scope.description: Canada-first gap-targeted demand research for a durable federal-government program with concrete Arctic operational outcomes, committed investment, implementation locations, and current official evidence.

source.title: Northern Operational Support Hubs (NOSH)
source.locator: Vision, Hubs and nodes, Site locations, Arctic and northern investment, Engagement and consultation, and Contact us sections
source.summary: The current official program page documents a $2.67 billion, 2024-2044 network of Arctic hubs and nodes intended to improve Canadian Armed Forces presence, reach, mobility, responsiveness, logistical support, and year-round operations.

leads.evidenceLocator: Program vision, infrastructure and logistics model, confirmed locations, public investment, partner commitments, and intended operational outcomes
followUpQuestions: Should the reviewer expose the hub and node locations in the public summary or retain them as evidence detail?
Should future procurement notices and individual site projects become separate demand sources when their scopes and delivery authorities are public?
Does the derived Arctic Domain Awareness mapping adequately describe the program's enabling role without overstating it as a sensing requirement?
leads.title: Northern Operational Support Hubs: Arctic operational reach and sustainment
candidateRequirements: Canada requires a distributed network of northern hubs, nodes, transportation corridors, infrastructure, logistics, pre-positioned resources, and quickly activated multi-modal support so the Canadian Armed Forces can respond faster, remain longer, and operate effectively year-round across the Arctic.

Northern operational infrastructure should support military requirements while enabling collaboration with Indigenous, territorial, provincial, municipal, federal, industry, academic, and allied partners and providing durable dual-use community benefits where feasible.
